note: Golden fixtures (plan 4.2). A case counts a row when its fix date is before `capture` AND its fixed version was in
the archive at `archiveAt` (the `archive` file, from snapshot.ubuntu.com / snapshot.debian.org), so later OSV
records never move a frozen fixture. Kernel rows are not counted (the pill never counts a pending kernel).
Stock ubuntu:24.04 (sha256:fe81560990fa..., created 2026-10-25) and stock debian:12 both flag apt for
CVE-2026-109518 (CVSS 4.0 High): USN-8996-1 2026-11-04 13:37 UTC, apt 2.8.4ubuntu0.1 published to noble-security
2026-11-04 14:25 UTC (Launchpad); Debian apt 2.6.2 in the bookworm archive at the capture snapshot. Both images
predate the fix, so both are real pending updates at capture time.
debian:12.0: the S0 prototype (scripts/match.py, all severities) flags 18 sources: these 11 plus gcc-12,
libgcrypt20, libtasn1-6, sed, shadow, tar, util-linux, whose fixes are all Medium or Low (D6 drops them).
Alpine (apk) cases: the fixture is the app's Pro probe output (P:/V:/o: lines of /lib/apk/db/installed) from a stock
image, matched against the SHIPPED rows exactly as the app does (introduced <= installed < fixed, per origin the
highest version, kernel origins not counted). OSV Alpine has no fix dates and there is no archive snapshot, so a
frozen image legitimately gains hits as fixes land: these cases are `atLeast`, measured 2026-11-05 against the
local S4 build, and 3 or more unexpected origins still fail (EXTRA_HIT_LIMIT, as for exact cases). alpine:3.20
(3.20.10, sha256:d9e853e87e55...) flags nothing and is `exact: []`: 3.20 is end of life, so it is the Alpine
false-positive gate (an unexpected origin warns, 3 or more fail). alpine:3.20.0
(sha256:77726ef6b57d..., May 2024) flags musl, openssl, zlib; alpine:latest (3.24.2, sha256:294b683cb724...) flags
EL (rpm, S5) cases: the fixture is the app's Pro probe rpm listing (NAME, EPOCHNUM:VERSION-RELEASE, ARCH, SOURCERPM,
MODULARITYLABEL) from a stock image as uid 1000, matched against the shipped rows exactly as the app does (per binary
the highest EVR; the module-stream rule; findings grouped by source rpm; kernel rows not counted), counting rows whose
advisory is dated before `capture` (EL advisories carry their date). almalinux:9 (9.8, sha256:245f8aab832f...)
flags nothing on alma-9 (the EL false-positive gate). almalinux:9.2 (sha256:09fdb3db0975..., July 2023) and
rockylinux:9 (the Docker library image, 9.3, sha256:d7be1c094cc5..., November 2023; against the RHEL data, as the
app matches Rocky) flag their known sets; every flagged binary had an upgrade at or above the fix in the image's own
rockylinux/rockylinux:9 (RESF's image, 9.8, sha256:8101994123cf...) is behind RHEL by months and flags its set too.
repositories (`dnf repoquery` in the image, 2026-11-05). The two synthetic php:8.2 listings (no image) prove the
stream rule: php:8.3 rows (8.3.36 > 8.2.33) and php:8.1 rows never match a php:8.2 module host.
